issues.description: The problem statement instructs that the SealSaloon.stock should be initialized to a default value in the SealSaloon constructor (instance initialization), but elsewhere (explicit note) requires the stock attribute to be static and shared across all instances. This is contradictory: a static shared field should not be described as being initialized in the instance constructor. Students could be confused whether to declare stock as an instance final field initialized in the constructor or as a static field initialized at declaration/static initializer.
issues.suggestedFix: Clarify the specification: decide whether stock is an instance final field or a static shared field. If stock must be shared across all SealSaloon instances, update the problem statement to state that stock is a static (e.g., private static final Stock) and should be initialized at declaration or in a static initializer (not in the instance constructor). If it should be an instance final field, remove the note requiring it to be static. Provide a short example snippet in the statement showing the intended declaration (e.g., private static final Stock stock = new Stock();).
